title: DNS and network troubleshooting from Linux
description: Diagnose DNS, routing, and connectivity issues from a Linux terminal.

data.text: When a server cannot reach another server, the cause is usually DNS, routing, or a firewall. Linux has built-in tools for diagnosing each layer of the network stack. Knowing which tool to use at each step turns a confusing network problem into a systematic investigation.

DNS is the phone book of the internet. It maps hostnames to IP addresses. If DNS fails, your server cannot find the services it needs. Routing determines the path packets take across networks. Firewalls can block traffic even when DNS and routing are correct.

The dig command queries DNS servers directly. It shows the answer section, which contains the IP address, and additional information about the DNS resolution path. Use dig to verify that a hostname resolves to the expected IP address and that the correct DNS server is being used.

data.code:
dig example.com
dig @8.8.8.8 example.com
# Check local DNS resolver
cat /etc/resolv.conf

data.text: The ip command replaces the older ifconfig and route commands. It shows network interfaces, IP addresses, and the routing table. The route command or ip route show displays where packets will go. The traceroute command shows the path packets take to a destination and where they stop.

data.code:
ip addr show
ip route show
traceroute -T -p 443 example.com
mtr -rw -c 10 example.com

data.text: The ping command tests basic IP connectivity using ICMP. Some servers block ICMP, so a lack of ping response does not always mean the server is down. The nc (netcat) command tests TCP and UDP connectivity. curl tests HTTP and HTTPS connectivity. Together, these tools isolate whether the problem is at the network, transport, or application layer.

data.title: Hosts file override
data.text: The /etc/hosts file takes precedence over DNS. If a server resolves to the wrong IP, check /etc/hosts first. This is a common issue after migrations or when local overrides are left in place.

data.title: Key Takeaways
items: Use dig to verify DNS resolution
Use ip and traceroute to inspect routing
Use ping, nc, and curl to test connectivity at different layers
Check /etc/hosts before assuming DNS is correct
Firewalls can block traffic even when routing and DNS are correct
